title: Bourgain booster theorem
statement: There exist positive real constants $C,D$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, every real-valued function $f$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, and every real $K$ with $I(f)\leq K$ and $1/100\leq\operatorname{Var}_P(f)$, there is a real number $\tau$ such that $e^{-CK^2}\leq|\tau|$ and $|\tau|$ is at most the probability of the event that an outcome $x$ admits a set of coordinates $T$ with $|T|\leq DK$ for which either $\tau>0$ and $\mathbb E_P f+\tau\leq E_Tf(x)$, or $\tau<0$ and $E_Tf(x)\leq\mathbb E_P f+\tau$.
hypotheses_covered: There exist real constants C and D with 0 < C and 0 < D
Product P of n finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and coordinate weights summing to one
Function f takes only the values −1 and 1
replaced: There are absolute $C,D>0$ such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, every $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, and every real $K$ satisfying $I(f)\le K$ and $\operatorname{Var}_P(f)\ge1/100$, there exists $\tau\in\mathbb R$ with $e^{-CK^2}\le|\tau|\le\Pr_P(\exists T\subseteq[n],\ |T|\le DK:\ (T,x)\text{ is a }\tau\text{-booster})$. A $\tau$-booster has $E_Tf(x)\ge\mathbb E_Pf+\tau$ for $\tau>0$, or $E_Tf(x)\le\mathbb E_Pf+\tau$ for $\tau<0$.
